verdict: Avoid new cut-and-polished diamond exposure in Jaipur; lend only to organised, domestic-retail-linked jewellers with tight stock-and-receivable controls, and decline export-oriented CPD processors until US tariff and Rajasthan demand signals clear.
title: Jaipur Cut & Polished Diamonds / Gems & Jewellery: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
**A Jaipur CPD unit buys rough, gets it cut and polished (largely by job-work karigars), and sells polished stones to wholesalers and exporters — so cash is tied in rough stock and receivables, not in plant.** Value sits in grading, assortment and buyer relationships, not in the cutting itself; the industry is 'highly fragmented and low value addition in nature leading to stiff competition' with 'modest profitability' [9]. Almost all revenue is export-linked — one rated peer shows 'almost 90% of total revenues from export earnings' [9] — so the rupee and the buyer's market drive the P&L, not local demand. Capex is light; a rated peer runs with 'no major capital expenditure (capex) plans' and controlled working capital [8]. So when a proposal lands, check the rough-inventory days and receivable days first; if either is rising faster than sales, ask why before touching the limit. ## What has changed now
**The export engine is the risk: 'more than 75% of CPD players expect volumes to be impacted due to US tariffs' and their 'ability to pass on the additional costs will remain a key monitorable' [4].** That ICRA survey is dated June 2025 — treat it as old but directionally live, since the US is the largest market [5]. Broader gems & jewellery exports were 'falling' at the start of FY26 [6]. Locally, Rajasthan GST collections are -4.7% Apr-to-date versus India +6.1% and electricity demand +4.0% versus India +9.5% [D] — two independent local stress signals. Nationally, bank credit is +33.0% YoY against output +3.8% [D], so money is chasing this trade faster than it is earning. The one bright spot is domestic retail: a lab-grown brand has just opened a Jaipur store targeting 100 outlets in five years [2], and organised retail expansion is cited as a demand driver [6]. ## Where to grow, and where not to
**Pursue domestic-retail-linked jewellers and organised showroom formats with real sell-through; avoid pure export CPD processors and job-work-dependent units.** The Jaipur-specific news flow is thin — one store opening [2] and a real-estate/JDA story [1] that says nothing about diamonds — so lean on first principles and peers here. For retail jewellers, ask for GST-wise monthly sales, gold/diamond metal-loan position and stock-turn; for any CPD processor still seeking limits, require the US-buyer split and tariff pass-through evidence [4]. Decline borrowers whose top three customers exceed 61% of revenue — that is the concentration a rated peer carries [8] — unless you are comfortable with single-buyer risk. ## How to grow safely
**Structure short: cash credit against stock with a drawing-power formula, receivables-backed limits, and no clean export packing credit beyond one cycle.** Take monthly stock and debtor statements, quarterly GST returns, and a certificate of rough-plus-polished inventory valued at cost. Covenant on margin: a drop in operating margin below 3% or a revenue decline is an explicit rating trigger in the sector [10], so write it in. For retail, take monthly sales and stock-turn; for processors, take monthly export-realisation and buyer-wise outstanding. Keep tenors under 12 months and insist on promoter personal guarantee. ## Early-warning signs
**Watch receivable days, rough-stock build and buyer concentration — these move before default.** If debtor days stretch beyond the sanctioned cycle, cut drawing power immediately. If inventory rises while sales fall, ask for a physical stock audit. If a single US buyer crosses half of revenue, reduce exposure. If the promoter seeks fresh capex funding, decline — the sector runs on light capex [8] and debt-funded expansion is a stated rating risk [10].
watch: Receivable days exceed sanctioned cycle -> freeze drawing power and seek buyer-wise ageing
GST turnover falls below bank-statement sales -> ask for reconciliation and re-rate limit
Margin below 3% or revenue decline -> invoke covenant review per rating trigger [10]
Continued negative GST growth vs India [D] -> pause new CPD limits in Jaipur
